Maria (finance): Heads up — invoice INV-APAC-342 shows a weird carryforward and a duplicated reservation SKU. Negative carryforward of -$187k plus two GPU reservation lines with different unit prices. Can someone sanity-check?

Kevin (infra): Which commitment IDs are attached? Dedicated or pooled reservations?

Maria (finance): Quick snippet from the invoice: 
```
SKU | description | quantity | unit_price | amount
GPU_RESERVED_CAPACITY_APAC | Dedicated GPU reservation | 720 | $1.25 | $900.00
GPU_RESERVED_CAPACITY_APAC | Dedicated GPU reservation | 720 | $0.92 | $662.40
COMMITMENT_CARRYFWD_ADJ | Commitment carryforward | -1 | $-187000.00 | -$187000.00
```

Ashley (ops): That smells like a reallocation overlap — one line billed under the old commit, one under the new. Did we request a reassign recently? :thinking_face:

Maria (finance): Yes — reassign request CR-8921 last month to consolidate sandbox commits into corp-apac. Cloud rep acknowledged but flagged it might span billing windows.

Julian (sales): We should avoid negative carryforwards at invoice level. Could be timing + a credit. @billing-bot any ingestion logs?

billing-bot: Invoice INV-APAC-342 ingested 2026-03-03T02:14:00Z. Matched to projects: prod-apac, sandbox-apac, corp-apac. Found 3 reservation lines and 1 carryforward adj.

Kevin (infra): Run a quick BigQuery to join invoice lines to commitment assignments — want to see which commitment_ids map to each line. Try: 
```sql
SELECT invoice_id, sku, SUM(amount) AS total_amount, ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT commitment_id) AS commitments
FROM `redwood-billing.gcp.invoice_lines`
WHERE invoice_id='INV-APAC-342'
GROUP BY invoice_id, sku;
```

Maria (finance): Ran it. Output shows the GPU SKU tied to two different commitment_ids on the same invoice (commit-334 and commit-678).

Ashley (ops): That explains the two unit prices — pre-reassign rate (commit-334) vs post-reassign rate (commit-678). If the cloud invoicing pipeline doesn't collapse overlap windows, it will bill both. We need the commit change timeline.

Maria (finance): I dug into the commit change email thread. Timeline: request CR-8921 submitted 2026-02-18; cloud rep acknowledged 2026-02-20; internal tagging changed 2026-02-25; billing window ended 2026-02-28. So overlap could exist.

Kevin (infra): Also worth verifying Dedicated dashboard — sometimes a reservation migration can temporarily double-count vGPU reservations while migrating VMs. Can you check cluster allocation for that window?

Ashley (ops): I checked logs and capacity metrics: no persistent double provisioning. Peak allocation matched expected numbers. This looks purely invoicing-apportionment overlap, not real double-billing of resources.

Maria (finance): Drafted case text to cloud support: 
"Duplicate reservation line with differing unit rates (0.92 vs 1.25) and a large negative carryforward adjustment after commitment reassign CR-8921. Expected single apportionment to corp-apac commit. Please reconcile invoice INV-APAC-342 and issue credit if applicable. Including commit change timeline and BigQuery joins"

Julian (sales): Sounds good. Ask for pro-rated credit if they confirm overlap. Also request confirmation that future invoices will map to the single consolidated commit id.

Kevin (infra): Attaching the BigQuery CSV and commit change emails when opening the case. Also ask cloud whether their invoicing pipeline has a reconciliation pass for commit reassignments that straddle billing windows.

billing-bot: Case CASE-20933 created at 1748883555. Cloud rep assigned: rep-id=GCP-REP-44.

Maria (finance): Case opened and PR notes added. Marking P1 for finance reconciliation. Will follow up when cloud replies. Thanks team :pray:

Ashley (ops): FYI — I'll schedule a job to re-run the invoice -> commit join for the next two billing cycles to catch any residual mapping glitches.

Kevin (infra): Good call. If cloud refuses to credit, we'll need an internal adjustment and a post-mortem on commit reassign timing.

Maria (finance): Closing loop here for now. Will post updates in this thread once CASE-20933 responds.

End of thread.
